title: Implement line decoder (core UU bit manipulation)
description:
Implement the low-level per-line decode logic in src/decode.rs. This is the heart of the crate; everything else builds on it.

Function signature (private):
  fn decode_line(line: &[u8], out: &mut Vec<u8>) -> Result<usize, UuError>
  // line: raw bytes of ONE data line, with leading/trailing whitespace already stripped (including \r)
  // out: append decoded bytes here
  // returns: number of bytes appended (0 for terminator lines)

Algorithm:
1. Strip trailing \r if present (defensive — caller should have done this but be safe)
2. If line is empty, or first byte is backtick (0x60), or first byte is space (0x20): this is the zero-length terminator line. Append nothing, return Ok(0).
3. Read length byte: N = (line[0] - 32) & 0x3F. This is the number of decoded bytes this line should produce.
4. If N == 0: terminator. Return Ok(0).
5. Compute minimum encoded chars needed: encoded_needed = ((N + 2) / 3) * 4
6. If line[1..].len() < encoded_needed: right-pad with spaces (0x20) conceptually — do not mutate line; just treat missing bytes as 0x20.
7. Decode groups of 4 encoded bytes into 3 decoded bytes using the UU alphabet: decoded_byte = (a<<2)|(b>>4), etc. Both 0x20 and 0x60 decode to 6-bit value 0. Bytes outside 0x20..=0x5F and not 0x60 return Err(UuError::InvalidChar{...}).
8. Emit only min(3, remaining_N) bytes from each group, stopping when N bytes have been emitted.
9. Ignore any encoded chars beyond encoded_needed (long lines are tolerated).

No begin/end parsing here. No allocation beyond appending to out.

Test oracle: Python's uu module (stdlib) or the UNIX uuencode/uudecode utilities.
Specifically test:
- Full 45-byte line (M prefix)
- Short final line (1, 2, 3 bytes)
- Line with trailing spaces stripped (shorter than length implies)
- Terminator as backtick, as space, as blank
- Both 0x20 and 0x60 as zero in data positions
- Byte outside valid range -> Err
- Do NOT test begin/end framing here
